entry: American financier and con artist. Madoff founded a penny stock brokerage in 1960 that grew into Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities, and he was at one time chairman of the [[Nasdaq]] stock exchange. He ran the largest-known [[Ponzi scheme]] in history, with almost $65 billion missing from client accounts. After his arrest in December 2008 he pleaded guilty to 11 federal felonies, and in 2009 he was sentenced to 150 years in prison.

American politician and activist. Sanders has been the senior U.S. senator from [[Vermont]] since 2007 and is the longest-serving independent in U.S. congressional history. He has caucused with the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and sought its presidential nomination in 2016 and 2020, finishing second both times. Describing himself as a democratic socialist, he has advocated universal healthcare, tuition-free tertiary education and a Green New Deal. He is credited with influencing a leftward shift in the Democratic Party after his 2016 campaign.

Discrete probability distribution of a single yes–no trial, such as a possibly biased coin toss. A random variable with this distribution takes the value 1 with probability p and the value 0 with probability 1 − p. Its mean is p and its variance is p(1 − p). It is a special case of the [[Binomial distribution|binomial distribution]] with one trial, named after Swiss mathematician [[Jacob Bernoulli]].

Principle of [[Fluid dynamics|fluid dynamics]] relating pressure, speed and height. For a fluid flowing horizontally, an increase in speed occurs with a decrease in pressure, so the highest speed occurs where the pressure is lowest. The principle is named after Swiss mathematician and physicist [[Daniel Bernoulli]], who published it in *Hydrodynamica* in 1738. [[Leonhard Euler]] derived Bernoulli's equation in its usual form in 1752. The principle can be derived from [[Isaac Newton]]'s second law of motion or from [[Conservation of energy|conservation of energy]], in which a gain in kinetic energy is balanced by a loss in potential and internal energy. It applies to isentropic flows, in which the effects of [[Turbulence|turbulence]] and other irreversible processes are small. The simple form applies to incompressible flows, such as most liquid flows and gases at low [[Mach number|Mach number]]. It underlies devices such as the Venturi meter and pitot-static tubes.

American record executive, songwriter and producer. Born in [[Detroit]], Gordy founded the [[Motown]] record label, which was the highest-earning African-American business for decades. As a songwriter he wrote hits including "Money (That's What I Want)", and as part of The Corporation he wrote songs for the [[The Jackson 5|Jackson 5]], including "I Want You Back". As a producer he signed acts including [[The Supremes]], [[Marvin Gaye]] and [[Stevie Wonder]]. He was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 1988.

Simple fleshy [[Fruit|fruit]] that develops from a single flower with one ovary. In botany, berries include [[Grape|grapes]], [[Tomato|tomatoes]], [[Cucumber|cucumbers]], [[Eggplant|eggplants]] and [[Banana|bananas]], but exclude culinary berries such as strawberries and raspberries. A berry is the most common type of fleshy fruit in which the entire outer layer of the ovary wall ripens into an edible pericarp. Its seeds are usually embedded in pulp rather than in a stone or pit. Many berries are edible, but others, such as the fruits of the potato and deadly nightshade, are poisonous to humans. Citrus fruits such as the [[Orange (fruit)|orange]] are a special kind of berry called a hesperidium, and gourd-family fruits are called pepos.

Japanese dark fantasy [[Manga|manga]] series created by Kentaro Miura. Set in a medieval Europe-inspired world, it follows the swordsman Guts, who seeks [[Revenge|revenge]] on Griffith, the leader of a mercenary group called the Band of the Hawk. The series began publication in 1989 in the seinen magazine *Monthly Animal House* and later appeared in *Young Animal*. After Miura's death the series resumed in 2022 under the supervision of Kouji Mori and Miura's assistants at Studio Gaga. Two [[Anime|anime]] series have adapted it, and more than 70 million copies were in circulation by August 2025.

German theater practitioner, playwright and poet. Coming of age during the [[Weimar Republic]], Brecht moved to Berlin in 1924 and wrote *The Threepenny Opera* (1928) with Kurt Weill. He became a leading theorist of epic theater, which he later preferred to call [[Dialectic|dialectical]] theater, and he developed the *Verfremdungseffekt* (alienation effect). After the Nazis came to power in 1933 he fled Germany, initially to [[Scandinavia]]. During [[World War II]] he moved to [[Southern California]], where he worked as a screenwriter while under FBI surveillance. In 1947 he testified before the House Un-American Activities Committee. He later settled in East Berlin, where he co-founded the Berliner Ensemble with his wife, the actress Helene Weigel.

English mathematician, philosopher and social critic. Russell was a founder of [[Analytic philosophy|analytic philosophy]] with Gottlob Frege, G. E. Moore and [[Ludwig Wittgenstein]]. With [[Alfred North Whitehead]] he wrote *Principia Mathematica*, a major attempt to reduce mathematics to logic. A [[Pacifism|pacifist]], he went to prison during [[World War I]]. He initially supported appeasing [[Adolf Hitler]]'s [[Nazi Germany]], but in 1943 he described war as a necessary "lesser of two evils". After World War II he criticized Stalinist totalitarianism, condemned U.S. involvement in the [[Vietnam War]] and became an advocate of nuclear disarmament. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950 "in recognition of his varied and significant writings in which he champions humanitarian ideals and freedom of thought".

Mineral composed of [[Beryllium|beryllium]] aluminum silicate, Be₃Al₂(SiO₃)₆. Well-known varieties include [[Emerald|emerald]] and aquamarine. Pure beryl is colorless, but impurities tint it green, blue, yellow, pink or red, with red the rarest. Its hexagonal crystals can reach several m in size. Beryl is an ore source of beryllium.

Chemical element with symbol Be and atomic number 4. Beryllium is a steel-gray, hard, strong, lightweight and brittle [[Alkaline earth metal|alkaline earth metal]]. It occurs naturally only in combination with other elements, mainly in [[Beryl|beryl]] and chrysoberyl. Its low density, 1.85 times that of water, and high stiffness make it useful for [[Aircraft|aircraft]] components, [[Missile|missiles]], [[Spacecraft|spacecraft]] and [[Satellite|satellites]]. Because it is relatively transparent to [[X-ray|X-rays]], it is the most common window material for X-ray equipment. Alloyed with [[Copper|copper]], it produces tools that are strong and do not create sparks. Inhaled dust is toxic and can cause berylliosis, a chronic allergic disease that in severe cases leads to heart failure and death. The world produces 220 tons a year, usually extracted from beryl.

Hostage siege at School Number One in Beslan, North Ossetia, [[Russia]], September 1–3, 2004. Militants sent by Chechen warlord Shamil Basayev held more than 1,100 hostages, including 777 children, for three days. Russian security forces stormed the building, and the siege ended with the deaths of 334 people, 186 of them children, and 31 attackers. It is considered the deadliest school shooting in history. Official accounts describe the attack as Islamist in nature. Criticism of the government's handling of the crisis has persisted, including allegations of disinformation and censorship in the news media.

Family of special functions that are solutions to a particular ordinary differential equation. Bessel functions commonly appear in problems of [[Wave|wave]] motion, heat conduction and other phenomena with circular or cylindrical symmetry. They are named after German astronomer and mathematician Friedrich Bessel, who studied them systematically in 1824. When the order is an integer they are called cylinder functions and arise in solving [[Laplace's equation|Laplace's equation]] in cylindrical coordinates; half-integer orders give spherical Bessel functions.

Type of radioactive decay in which a nucleus emits a [[Beta particle|beta particle]] and becomes an isobar of the original nuclide. In beta-minus decay a neutron becomes a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino. In beta-plus decay a proton becomes a neutron, emitting a positron and a neutrino. The process results from the [[Weak interaction|weak force]] and moves unstable nuclei toward a more stable ratio of protons to neutrons. It occurs in about 97% of known unstable isotopes.

Family of continuous probability distributions on the interval [0, 1], controlled by two positive shape parameters, α and β. The beta distribution is suitable for modeling percentages and proportions. In [[Bayesian inference]] it is the conjugate prior for the [[Bernoulli distribution|Bernoulli]], [[Binomial distribution|binomial]], negative binomial and [[Geometric distribution|geometric]] distributions. Its generalization to multiple variables is the Dirichlet distribution.

High-energy, high-speed electron or positron emitted by a radioactive nucleus during [[Beta decay|beta decay]]. Beta particles are a form of [[Ionizing radiation|ionizing radiation]]. For radiation protection they are considered more ionizing than [[Gamma ray|gamma rays]] but less ionizing than [[Alpha particle|alpha particles]], producing roughly 100 ion pairs per cm in air. Beta particles with an energy of 0.5 MeV have a range of about 1 m in air, and they cannot pass through clothing or thin metal sheets. Beta emitters are used in radiotherapy, and [[Positron|positron]] emission tomography (PET) scans rely on beta-plus decay.

Practice of chewing areca nut with slaked lime and betel leaves, usually as a betel quid. The nut contains arecoline, a [[Stimulant|stimulant]] alkaloid, and the mixture may include flavorings such as cardamom or menthol. The preparation is spat out and causes permanent red stains on the teeth. The practice originated in [[Southeast Asia]], and its spread is closely tied to the expansion of the [[Austronesian peoples|Austronesian peoples]], reaching [[Micronesia]], [[South Asia]] and [[Madagascar]] in prehistoric times. It is addictive and is linked to oral and esophageal cancers and cardiovascular disease.

Red supergiant star in the constellation [[Orion (constellation)|Orion]], usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky. Its radius is 640 to 764 times that of the Sun. If it were at the center of the [[Solar System]], its surface would lie beyond the [[Asteroid belt|asteroid belt]] and engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. Its apparent magnitude varies between +0.0 and +1.6 over a main period near 400 days, the widest range of any first-magnitude star. It dimmed noticeably from October 2019 and by February 2020 had dropped in brightness by a factor of about 3. Infrared observations found no significant change in its luminosity, suggesting dust around the star caused the dimming. It is expected to end its life in a [[Supernova|supernova]] most likely within the next 100,000 years. It may have a companion star, Betelgeuse B or Siwarha, though this is not fully confirmed.

City in the [[West Bank]], Palestine, about 10 km south of Jerusalem (pop., 2017: 28,591). Its economy is strongly linked to tourism, especially at [[Christmas]], when pilgrims visit the Church of the Nativity, revered as the site of the birth of [[Jesus]]. The Hebrew Bible identifies Bethlehem as the birthplace of [[David]]. After the Ottoman Empire ended in World War I, the city was part of [[Mandatory Palestine]]. Israel occupied the West Bank in the [[Six-Day War]] of 1967. Under the [[Oslo Accords]] Bethlehem was designated Area A, nominally under Palestinian control.

American actress of film, television and stage. Davis was known for playing unsympathetic, sardonic characters, and her romantic dramas were among her greatest successes. She won the [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for Best Actress twice, for *Dangerous* (1935) and *Jezebel* (1938), and she was the first person to accrue 10 Academy Award nominations for acting. Her career was revived by *All About Eve* (1950), often cited as her best performance. Her last Oscar nomination came for *What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?* (1962), co-starring [[Joan Crawford]]. She won an Emmy Award for *Strangers: The Story of a Mother and Daughter* (1979) and was the first female president of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

American actress, singer and comedian. Midler came to prominence in 1970 singing at the Continental Baths, a gay bathhouse in [[New York City]]. Her recordings include the hits "The Rose" and "Wind Beneath My Wings", and she has sold over 30 million records worldwide. She won [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards]] for Best New Artist and for Record of the Year with "Wind Beneath My Wings". Her starring role in *The Rose* (1979) earned her a Golden Globe and an Academy Award nomination. She received a Tony Award for the 2017 Broadway revival of *Hello, Dolly!*.

Animated [[Cartoon|cartoon]] character created by Max Fleischer for Fleischer Studios. A canine-inspired singer drawn by Grim Natwick appeared in *Dizzy Dishes* (1930), and over time the character evolved into Betty Boop. She was featured in 90 theatrical cartoons between 1930 and 1939, released by [[Paramount Pictures]]. A caricature of a Jazz Age flapper, she was made more modest in the mid-1930s under the [[Hays Code|Hays Code]], and she was overshadowed by other Fleischer series. She remains one of the world's best-known cartoon characters.

American [[Feminism|feminist]] writer and activist. Her 1963 book *The Feminine Mystique* is often credited with sparking the second wave of American feminism. In 1966 she co-founded the National Organization for Women (NOW) and was elected its first president. She organized the 1970 Women's Strike for Equality, and the march she led in New York City alone attracted over 50,000 people. In 1971 she helped establish the National Women's Political Caucus, and she supported the proposed Equal Rights Amendment. Her later book *The Second Stage* (1981) criticized what she saw as the extremist excesses of some feminists. She remained active in politics and advocacy until the late 1990s.

American actress and comedian. A pioneer of early television, she was known for appearances in [[Sitcom|sitcoms]], sketch comedy and [[Game show|game shows]]. She produced the sitcom *Life with Elizabeth* (1953–1955), becoming the first woman to do so. She was the first woman to win the Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Game Show Host. Her best-known roles were Sue Ann Nivens on *The Mary Tyler Moore Show* and Rose Nylund on *The Golden Girls*. She won seven Emmy Awards and twice earned a Guinness World Record for the longest TV career by a female entertainer.

American teen drama television series. Created by Darren Star and produced by Aaron Spelling, *Beverly Hills, 90210* ran for 10 seasons on Fox, from 1990 to 2000. It follows twins Brandon and Brenda Walsh, who move from Minneapolis to Beverly Hills as they make the transition from high school to college and adult life. The show addressed topics including date rape, [[Homophobia|homophobia]], [[Alcoholism|alcoholism]], [[Domestic violence]] and [[Racism|racism]]. It is credited with creating or popularizing the teen soap genre. Its stars Jason Priestley and [[Luke Perry]] became teen idols.
